name: Diffuse Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse thickening and hyperkeratosis of the palms and soles
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia with orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
Exclusion of acquired causes of palmoplantar keratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diffuse palmoplantar hyperkeratosis plus either positive family history or supportive histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse hyperkeratosis of palms and soles
searchTerms: thickened rough skin on palms and soles
widespread hard skin on hands and feet
extensive palm and sole skin thickening

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fissuring and painful cracks in palmoplantar skin
searchTerms: cracked, painful skin on palms and soles
painful skin cracks on hands and feet
excessive sweating on hands and feet
overactive sweat glands in hands and feet

common.notes: Thickened, brittle nails may be observed
Due to fissures and thickened skin
searchTerms: pain on putting pressure on feet

occasional.notes: Often due to fissures and skin barrier disruption
searchTerms: skin infections from bacteria or fungi

occasional.symptomName: Hyperkeratosis extending to dorsal aspects of hands and feet
occasional.notes: Less common extension beyond palms and soles
searchTerms: thick skin spreading to backs of hands and feet
hyperkeratosis extending beyond palms and soles
skin thickening on dorsal hands and feet

occasional.notes: Focal areas of thickening within diffuse plaques
searchTerms: small pits or spots in thickened skin

rare.notes: May lead to autoamputation in severe cases
searchTerms: thickened skin on palms/soles with constricting bands

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia and orthokeratotic hyperkeratosis
Negative fungal cultures to exclude tinea
imaging: Not typically required; imaging may be used to assess secondary complications
genetic: Mutations in genes such as KRT1, KRT9, or others depending on subtype
other: Clinical examination revealing diffuse thickening of palms and soles with fissures

distinguishingFeatures: Nail dystrophy more severe and early onset

redFlags: Rapid progression of keratoderma with ulceration
Development of constricting bands leading to digital ischemia
Signs of secondary infection such as fever or purulent discharge
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
